modules.title: Change detection
modules.question: What changed in the stored data and in RUMIN's records?
modules.method: Changes between consecutive current values (relative for levels, exchange rates and prices; percentage points for series already in percent), tested against configurable thresholds; superseded values against their revisions; edges the latest graph build added, changed or retired; the headline between two executions of a scenario.
limitations: Only what is stored is analysed: nothing is fetched or filled in.
Observed changes and model interpretations are separate findings.

modules.title: Trend, volatility and unusual change
modules.question: How has a series behaved over its latest window, against its own history?
modules.method: Least-squares trend with a t test, standard deviation of changes ranked among earlier windows, modified z-score of the latest change (exact decimals).
limitations: Descriptive statistics of the stored history; never a forecast.

modules.title: Exposure analysis
modules.question: Which economic variables reach an entity, through which validated relationships?
modules.method: Direct, via-industry and upstream (at most two `influences` hops) paths over current, validated edges of the latest completed build; counterparties and context listed apart; the models able to simulate each path and the series that measure each variable.
limitations: A stated exposure says that an entity is exposed, never how much.
Every sample relationship is a model assumption; none is evidence-backed.

modules.title: Contribution analysis
modules.question: What drives a simulated result, and what does it rest on?
modules.method: Each line's stored contributions per change (Shapley credits of the model runs), as amounts, points of the baseline and shares of the change; residual checked; per-unit effects; stored sensitivity rankings; the runs' assumptions and the user's figures.
limitations: Conditional on the scenario's figures and assumptions: not a forecast.
Ratios (margin, coverage) are not attributed.

modules.title: Observed change through the models
modules.question: What would the stored scenario's models say about the change just observed?
modules.method: The latest observed change of a series recorded as a related measure of a scenario variable, applied alone to the stored scenario version and run as a preview.
limitations: Computed on request and never stored; the series and the variable differ, as the curator states.

modules.title: Insights and briefs
modules.question: What should a reader know, and what should they look at next?
modules.method: Documented rules fill sentence templates with computed values and attach the evidence chain, facts, assumptions, limitations and rule-based next steps; the entity brief gathers every finding about one entity as structured facts.
limitations: No insight without an evidence chain; no free text is generated.

signals.name: Exposure breadth
signals.question: How many economic variables reach this entity through validated relationships?
signals.definition: The number of distinct economic variables on at least one validated exposure path to the entity, split by channel (costs, revenue, financing), by directness (direct, via the industry, upstream) and by evidence status.
signals.method: Count the variables and paths returned by the exposure analysis (validated edges of the latest completed build; at most two `influences` hops upstream).
signals.inputs: Knowledge-graph edges: affects_costs, affects_revenue, affects_financing, influences, in_industry.
limitations: Counts relationships, not money: two exposures with equal counts can differ by orders of magnitude.
Only what the graph states is counted; an exposure the graph does not record is invisible.

signals.name: Dependency
signals.question: Do the entity's stated exposures depend on one variable?
signals.definition: The largest share of the entity's exposure paths that pass through a single variable, and its supply and credit counterparties by kind.
signals.method: For each variable, count the exposure paths that contain it; divide the largest count by the number of paths. Concentrated when the share is at or above the threshold.
signals.inputs: The exposure paths; supplies_to and lends_to edges.
limitations: A share of relationships, not of costs or revenue.
Supply and credit relationships say nothing about size or terms.

signals.name: Trend
signals.question: Has the series been rising or falling over the latest window?
signals.definition: The ordinary least-squares slope of the latest window of values against their period, with its t statistic.
signals.method: slope = Σ(x−x̄)(y−ȳ) / Σ(x−x̄)²; t = slope / standard error. A direction is called only when |t| exceeds the two-sided critical value of Student's t with n−2 degrees of freedom at the chosen level; otherwise there is no clear direction.
signals.inputs: The latest window of current stored values (5 years, 8 quarters, 12 months or 20 trading days by default).
limitations: Describes the window; it is not a forecast.
The test assumes independent, normally distributed residuals, which economic series often are not; small windows have little power.

signals.name: Volatility
signals.question: Is the series moving more than it usually does?
signals.definition: The sample standard deviation of the changes in the latest window, compared with every earlier window of the same length in the series' own history.
signals.method: Changes are relative (percent) for levels, exchange rates and prices and in percentage points for series already in percent. The latest window's standard deviation is ranked among all windows; high when its percentile is at or above the threshold.
signals.inputs: Changes between consecutive current stored values.
limitations: Compares the series with its own past only.
Overlapping windows are not independent; the percentile is descriptive.

signals.name: Unusual change
signals.question: Is the latest change unusual against the series' earlier changes?
signals.definition: The modified z-score of the latest change against all earlier changes.
signals.method: M = 0.6745 × (x − median) / MAD (Iglewicz and Hoaglin, 1993), where MAD is the median absolute deviation of the earlier changes. Unusual when |M| is at or above the threshold; undefined when MAD is zero.
signals.inputs: Changes between consecutive current stored values.
limitations: Unusual is not wrong: a real event can produce an unusual change, and data quality is judged separately by the ingestion rules.
Needs enough earlier changes to be meaningful.

signals.name: Scenario sensitivity
signals.question: In the latest stored execution for this company, which change moves the result most, and by how much per unit?
signals.definition: Each change's contribution to the headline line (profit before tax, else operating profit), its share of the line's change, and its effect per 1 % (or per percentage point) of the change; with the stored one-at-a-time ranking when an analysis exists.
signals.method: Read from the execution's stored results: contributions are the models' Shapley credits per change. Per unit = contribution ÷ size of the change.
signals.inputs: A completed Scenario Lab execution and its stored sensitivity analyses.
limitations: Per-unit effects are averages over the scenario's change, not slopes: the models are not linear (hedges, lags, compounding).
Conditional on the scenario's figures and assumptions.

rules.title: Observed change
rules.purpose: The latest change of a series or instrument meets its threshold.

rules.title: Observed change on an exposure variable
rules.purpose: A detected change in a series recorded as a related measure of a variable that the graph states reaches companies; names the companies, claims no effect.

rules.title: Unusual change
rules.purpose: The latest change is unusual against earlier changes (modified z-score).

rules.title: Trend
rules.purpose: The latest window rises or falls with a t statistic beyond the critical value.

rules.title: High volatility
rules.purpose: The latest window moves more than most earlier windows.

rules.title: Data revision
rules.purpose: A stored value was replaced by a revised value.

rules.title: Simulated impact
rules.purpose: The headline result of the latest stored execution for a company.

rules.title: Contributions to a line
rules.purpose: A line's change split by the scenario's changes, from stored contributions.

rules.title: Effect per unit of a change
rules.purpose: Each change's contribution to the headline divided by its size.

rules.title: Largest sensitivity
rules.purpose: The quantity with the largest spread in a stored sensitivity analysis.

rules.title: Change between executions
rules.purpose: How the headline moved between two executions of the same scenario.

rules.title: Observed change through the models
rules.purpose: The latest observed change of a related series, applied to a stored scenario's figures and models: a model interpretation, computed on request and not stored.

rules.title: Relationship change
rules.purpose: An exposure-relevant edge the latest graph build added, changed or retired.

rules.title: Shared driver
rules.purpose: A variable that reaches two or more companies through validated relationships (at most 12, those reaching the most companies; the exposure matrix shows every one).

rules.title: Stated exposure
rules.purpose: A variable that reaches an entity through validated relationships.

rules.title: Concentrated dependency
rules.purpose: At least the threshold share of an entity's exposure paths (50 % by default) pass through one variable.

rules.title: Supply and credit relationships
rules.purpose: The entity's suppliers, customers, lenders and borrowers in the graph.

rules.title: What is and is not covered
rules.purpose: Which of an entity's exposures are simulated, simulatable and backed by data.

rules.title: Stored data
rules.purpose: How much stored data the analysis can use, and what cannot be computed without it.

thresholds.name: relative_change_percent
thresholds.label: Change in a level or exchange rate
thresholds.rationale: A round, deliberately high default for annual averages, so that only large movements are reported. It is a filter for attention, not a statement that smaller changes do not matter; lower it to see more.

thresholds.name: point_change
thresholds.label: Change in a rate or a percentage
thresholds.rationale: Series already expressed in percent (inflation, growth, interest rates, shares of GDP) are compared in percentage points, never in percent of themselves. One point is a round default for annual data.

thresholds.name: price_move_percent
thresholds.label: Move in a daily close
thresholds.rationale: Day-to-day moves of 5 % or more in a close. Ingestion already flags moves above 40 % as possible data errors; this threshold is for attention, not for quality.

thresholds.name: anomaly_score
thresholds.label: Unusual change (modified z-score)
thresholds.rationale: Iglewicz and Hoaglin (1993) recommend treating modified z-scores above 3.5 as potential outliers. The score uses the median and the median absolute deviation, so one earlier extreme change does not hide the next.

thresholds.name: trend_significance
thresholds.label: Trend test level
thresholds.rationale: A direction is called only when the slope's t statistic exceeds the two-sided critical value of Student's t at this level. The test assumes independent, normally distributed residuals; economic series often violate this, so a called trend describes the window, not a law.

thresholds.name: volatility_high_percentile
thresholds.label: High volatility
thresholds.rationale: Volatility is compared with the series' own history: the latest window is called high when its standard deviation is at or above this percentile of every earlier window of the same length.

thresholds.name: dependency_share_percent
thresholds.label: Concentrated dependency
thresholds.rationale: An entity's stated exposures are called concentrated when at least this share of its exposure paths pass through one variable. It counts relationships, not money.

thresholds.name: min_history
thresholds.label: Changes needed for a baseline
thresholds.rationale: Anomaly and volatility compare the latest change with earlier ones; with fewer than this many earlier changes the comparison is not made, and the result says so.

thresholds.name: window
thresholds.label: Window (periods)
thresholds.rationale: Periods used for the trend and the latest volatility window. Left empty, it follows the frequency: 5 years, 8 quarters, 12 months or 20 trading days.

grades.statement: Rests on stored observations, exact calculations on them and RUMIN's own records.
Rests on relationships stated by a cited external source (evidence-backed); RUMIN transcribed them and did not measure them.
Rests on relationships written by a RUMIN curator with their reasoning recorded; not an external source.
Rests on stored model outputs: deterministic results of the stated inputs and assumptions, not forecasts.
Rests on at least one relationship recorded as a model assumption: an assumed effect with a written rationale, not an empirical finding.
Rests on at least one relationship declared in supplied data that RUMIN could not check.

notes: Insights are produced by documented rules from stored data, validated graph relationships and stored simulations; no text is generated by a language model.
The evidence grade is the weakest step of an insight's chain. It is not a probability.
Observed changes and model interpretations are separate findings, labelled as such.
Simulated values hold only under their scenario's inputs and assumptions; they are not forecasts.
